npu-computing-forecast.title: Ascend NPU Resource Prediction
npu-computing-forecast.summary: A Huawei collaboration on reproducible experiments, monitoring, and resource prediction for recommendation and language models on Ascend NPUs, supporting workload co-location and better cluster utilization.

images.dataOrderAllocatorComparison: Memory comparison across data orders and allocator settings

projectIntro: Explores resource prediction methods using task configuration, model structure, and data features to estimate hardware usage, TTFT/TPOT, and KV cache. Investigates GNNs to improve generalization through model structure.
Studies real training and inference workloads to understand Ascend hardware and its software ecosystem, reporting firsthand resource and performance issues to Huawei.
personalWork: Independently built a configuration-driven data collection framework for TorchRec, DeepCTR, Torch-RecHub, and RecSDK, extending it to LLaMA Factory, vLLM, and multiple NPUs.
Isolated data-order-driven memory peaks through controlled experiments, distinguished active from reserved memory, and validated expandable segments across models and tuning methods.
Built NPU monitoring with npu-smi, npu-exporter, and DCMI; cross-checked container CPU/memory with vmstat, sar, cgroup, and lxcfs, preserving raw traces.
Aligned per-rank training events with monitoring and separated initialization from training. Found and fixed ineffective gradient-checkpointing settings to protect data validity.
Built XGBoost predictors for recommendation workloads and LLM fine-tuning, estimating HBM, compute, and bandwidth usage from configuration, structure, and data features.

Compared features and evaluation splits, exploring direct memory prediction and corrections to static estimates. Some metrics reached R² 0.96+ for new configurations of known models; unseen models were evaluated separately.
Reported long-term observations to Huawei, including slow DLRM first epochs and fluctuating memory high-water marks.

crater.title: Crater Heterogeneous AI Platform
crater.summary: RAIDS Lab's Kubernetes platform for shared AI clusters, unifying scheduling, development environments, training and serving, images, data, and resource governance.

images.backendLogDiagnostics: Backend logs and slow SQL diagnostics

projectIntro: Our deployment serves 600+ users with 280+ accelerators, 5,600+ CPU cores, and 200+ daily jobs. Enterprise adoption has brought collaboration invitations; some components are deliverables under China's National Key R&D Program.
Combines a custom admission controller with Volcano scheduling, quotas, backfilling, CephFS limits, and bandwidth controls. Plans to migrate admission control to a Volcano extender integration.
Detects GPU-hoarding scripts that hold resources for long periods without doing meaningful work, helping curb misuse.
Replaces the lab's Slurm tooling with a web console and supports systems research in scheduling and distributed storage.
Supports snapshots, Buildx/Envd image builds, NFS/Ceph storage, and shared model and dataset management for reusable environments and assets.
Mostly completed an embedded Q&A agent to help users query and locate problems faster.
personalWork: As a **core maintainer**, helped shape requirements and designs, reviewed 40+ PRs, distinguished blockers from follow-ups, and mentored new contributors.
Diagnosed production issues involving RDMA devices, CephFS, slow jobs, container startup, and cluster egress, and helped drive fixes.
Early on, built and refined Jupyter, CUDA, and PyTorch images for the platform, simplifying setup and improving out-of-the-box usability.
Designed and built the Crater CLI framework and Agent Skills from scratch for users, scripts, and AI agents.
Turned user feedback into features and fixes, improving workflows, error messages, and usability.
Created development Skills for code, documentation, and releases, capturing engineering constraints, review lessons, and verification requirements.

crater-cli.title: Crater CLI
crater-cli.summary: A Go CLI subproject for operating Crater through AI agents, scripts, and related workflows.

projectIntro: Provides a new way to access and operate the Crater platform for script/CLI users and AI agents in the new era.
Gradually connecting the APIs of Crater modules...
personalWork: Provides architecture, spec, command, and review docs, using documentation-driven development for AI-era coding.
Provides multilingual Tab completion and survey-style interactive selection across shells.
Distributes Skills, supports non-interactive/formatted output, and defines error codes for agent use and troubleshooting.
Implements sandboxed network and storage access so tests do not affect real environments or cluster data.

Improves AI-generated code reliability with unit tests and a sandbox-based snapshot/golden-file mechanism that leaves reference examples for later AI coding and lets reviewers see real command output.
Designed from scratch, accumulating architecture design experience and real engineering reflections.

model-requirements-evaluator.title: Equivalent Modeling and Evaluation of Model Compute Requirements
model-requirements-evaluator.summary: Models inference-time resource requirements for LLMs across vendors' hardware. Given a model, GPU, concurrency, and latency needs, it produces deployment plans that satisfy the constraints.

projectIntro: Won third prize in the 2nd 'China Data Valley Huawei Cup' China Graduate Operating System Open Source Innovation Competition.
Decomposes large language model structure and uses mathematical methods to model the storage and compute requirements of each part of the model.
personalWork: Built a modern frontend with Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, and Element Plus, packaging backend capabilities into an interactive product.
Integrated ECharts and ECharts-GL to visualize latency, throughput, memory, and phase progress, showing how requirement changes affect deployment cost.

personal-homepage.title: Personal Homepage and Content System
personal-homepage.summary: This site is also a long-running frontend project for HR, interviewers, open-source peers, and students. It organizes job-search presentation, open-source activity, and related content into a maintainable static site.

projectIntro: Designed layouts for phones and desktops of different sizes, with multiple languages, light/dark themes, and animation levels; dark mode also dims overly bright screenshots so reading stays comfortable.
Maintained AI prompts and project specs that capture purpose, design principles, and constraints, so long-term iteration stays coherent.

Used AI to generate line art, light/dark concepts, and video, then recovered the camera path for the homepage FPV fly-through. The footage carries the space; copy, language, and theme stay in the site, so they can change without remaking the video. Gained experience in the problems of getting generated media into a product.
Separated presentation from content: the same components can render different entries, and one entry can appear on multiple pages, making changes and extensions easier.

kernel-analysis-thesis.title: GPU Operator Mapping and Fine-Grained Resource Prediction
kernel-analysis-thesis.summary: Studies how deep learning workloads use GPUs to understand resource needs and inform more efficient sharing. My BUAA Software Engineering undergraduate thesis, Research and Implementation of Fine-Grained Performance Analysis Techniques for Intelligent Computing Tasks.

images.yolov8ThroughputPrediction: YOLOv8 GPU compute throughput utilization prediction capability

projectIntro: Mapped ONNX operators to GPU kernel sequences, built kernel-level computation graphs, and studied mapping patterns to inform resource prediction.
Built a rule-based model to predict kernels and estimate compute and memory usage at low cost. Evaluated predictions to support future interference analysis and scheduling.
Automated batch profiling, trace parsing, and Nsight Compute data integration, with tools for mapping analysis, rule-model construction, and visualization.
